transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah… I came in because I keep getting these thoughts that I forgot something important. Like, I’ll think maybe I left my aunt’s medicine out wrong, or that I didn’t set up something safely in my classroom for the kids.

I mean, I know most of the time I probably did it fine, but then the doubt just pops back in my head. It’s kind of like when you’re trying to remember if you turned off the stove, except it’s not always the stove, and then I start thinking about all the little things. At school there are so many supplies and bins and scissors and glue sticks, and—sorry, I’m rambling—but it just keeps nagging at me even when I try to tell myself it’s okay.
When these thoughts come up, do you find yourself doing certain things, like checking, counting, or going through a routine to ease the worry?

Yeah… I do check things. Like before I leave the house, I’ll go back and look at the pill organizer, or the stove, sometimes more than once. And at school I’ll look over my lesson plans or the classroom stuff again before I leave.

Sometimes I’m not even physically checking, I’m just standing there replaying what I did in my head, like, “Okay, I put that away, I closed that, I set that up…” It reminds me of when my aunt used to make these little lists for groceries—sorry, that’s not really the point—but I kind of do that in my head.

I usually keep going until I feel calm enough to leave, but it can make me late sometimes.

Do you ever perform any actions or mental rituals that aren’t directly related to the things you’re worried about, like counting, repeating words, or following a specific routine to feel 'just right'?

Um… I’m not sure. I don’t think I do, like, counting or saying certain words or anything like that. At least not that I’ve noticed.

I mean, I do have routines, but I think everyone has some routines, right? Like when I’m setting up my classroom in the morning, I kind of like the desks a certain way, and the pencils in the little cups—actually the kids always mix them up by ten o’clock anyway, so it’s kind of pointless. But I don’t think it’s like I have to do some special thing to feel right.

It’s more… I just check the things I’m worried about, I guess. I might be missing what you mean though.
Do you ever have thoughts that upset you or make you feel uncomfortable, that you wish you could get rid of but keep coming back, even if you try not to think about them?

Yeah… yes, that’s pretty much it. It’s these nagging thoughts that I forgot something important, and they just kind of come back even when I try to push them away.

Like with my aunt’s medicine, I’ll think maybe I left it out wrong or didn’t put it where it should be. Or at school, I’ll worry I didn’t set up the classroom materials safely for the kids. And I’ll tell myself, “No, you probably handled it,” because usually I did, but then the doubt pops back in anyway.

It’s uncomfortable because it feels like I can’t quite trust my own memory, I guess. And then I get stuck on it longer than I want to.

Do you ever have any mental rituals or behaviors that you feel you must do to prevent something bad from happening, even if they aren’t directly related to the thing you’re worried about—like thinking certain words, mentally repeating numbers, or needing things to feel 'just right' in your mind?

I don’t think I do things like repeating numbers or special words, no. It’s more tied to the thing I’m worried about, if that makes sense.

Like before I leave the house, I’ll go back over the same stuff a few times—the pill organizer, the stove, things like that. And at school it’ll be my lesson plans or classroom materials. Sometimes I’m not even checking with my hands, I’m just standing there silently replaying, like, “I did this, I put that away…” until I feel calm enough to go.

It’s funny, my classroom has this one cabinet latch that never feels like it catches right—well, that’s probably not the point. But yeah, I keep going over it even when I know I probably already did it, and then I end up running late sometimes.
Do these thoughts ever feel intrusive or unwanted, like they don’t really fit with who you are, and do they cause you a lot of distress or interfere with your daily life?

Yeah… I think so. They feel unwanted, definitely. Like, I’ll be trying to go about my day and then it pops in—what if I left my aunt’s medicine out wrong, or what if something in the classroom wasn’t set up safely—and I don’t want to be thinking about it, but it keeps coming back.

And I know, logically, I probably handled it. I’m usually pretty careful. I mean, teachers kind of have to be careful with a room full of kids—sorry, that’s not really the point. But the doubt still gets in my head, and then I feel tense until I can reassure myself somehow.

It’s not like it ruins my whole life, but it does distress me, and it interferes some. It takes up time and makes me feel like I can’t just trust that I did what I needed to do.
